chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Shihab and Suleym al-Farra’, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever says this when it is evening, will be wrapped by a wing from the wings of Jibraeel (peace be upon him) until morning,
‘I entrust to Allah, the Exalted, the Supreme, the Majestic, the Magnificent, myself and the one whose matter concerns me.
I entrust to Allah my soul, which is feared, awed, and trembles before His greatness.
ai.seo_question: What is the evening supplication for protection and entrustment to Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Shia practice of *istiwda'* (entrustment) as a spiritual shield, promising divine protection through the presence of Archangel Jibraeel's wing. The supplication emphasizes the soul's fragility (*al-nafs al-marhub*) and total reliance on Allah's greatness, reflecting the theological concept of seeking refuge in the Divine during the transition from day to night. This practice underscores the importance of verbal dhikr as a means of securing spiritual safety and divine guardianship in daily life.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Shihab and Suleym Al Fara’a, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who says this when it is evening, would be wrapped up by a wing from the wings of Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> until the morning,
‘I entrust to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted, the Supreme, the Majestic, the Magnificent, myself and the ones whose matters are meaningful (important) to me.
I entrust myself to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, whom everything fears, and is awed by, and trembles to’
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Shahab and Sulaym al-Farra’ from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Whoever says in the evening, ‘I leave myself and all that is important to me, in trust of Allah, the Most High, the Most Glorious, the Most Great, from Whose greatness all things fear, worry and waver,’ three times, he will be wrapped up in a wing of the wings of Jibril, the Archangel, for protection until morning.’”
